test_title: PYST 35: RRB Group D - Mathematics (Held On: 12 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 32 minutes and pipe B can empty it in 48 minutes. If both the pipes are opened together, after how many minutes should pipe B be closed, so that the tank is filled in 60 minutes?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity of the tank = LCM of 32 and 48 = 96 units.

Efficiency of A = 96 ÷ 32 = +3 units/min, Efficiency of B = 96 ÷ 48 = −2 units/min.

Pipe A runs continuously for the full 60 minutes, filling 3 × 60 = 180 units.

Excess water that must be emptied by B = 180 − 96 = 84 units.

Time for which pipe B must operate = 84 ÷ 2 = 42 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 42 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A to fill the tank = 32 minutes.

Time taken by Pipe B to empty the tank = 48 minutes.

Total time to fill the tank = 60 minutes.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculations:**

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Time (minutes)**
 **Total Work (units)**
 **Efficiency (units/min)**
 
 

 Pipe A
 32
 96
 +3
 
 

 Pipe B
 48
 −2
 
 

⇒ Let Pipe B be closed after x minutes.

⇒ Since the tank is filled exactly in 60 minutes, Pipe A operates for the entire 60 minutes.

⇒ Total work done by Pipe A + Total work done by Pipe B = Tank Capacity

⇒ (3 × 60) + (−2 × x) = 96

⇒ 180 − 2x = 96

⇒ 2x = 180 − 96

⇒ 2x = 84

⇒ x = 42

⇒ Pipe B was kept open for 42 minutes before closing.

**∴ The correct answer is 42 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Basics

A pipe that fills the tank has a positive efficiency, while a pipe that empties it (a leak) has a negative efficiency. If an inlet fills in x hours and an outlet empties in y hours, the net work completed in 1 hour is (1/x − 1/y).

Total Work Concept

Total capacity of the cistern is typically assumed as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the time taken by all individual pipes. This converts the fractional work into whole numbers, making calculations easier and faster.

Alternating Pipes

When pipes operate alternately, treat one complete cycle (e.g., 2 minutes) as a single unit of work. Always be careful in the final cycle, as the tank may get fully filled by the positive pipe before the negative pipe opens again.
